correctness.rationale: The module-isomorphism relation is simultaneous GL₂(k)-conjugacy, so fixing a representative X leaves precisely its invertible centralizer acting on Y. For X=0, rational similarity gives q scalars, q nontrivial Jordan classes, q(q−1)/2 split regular classes and (q²−q)/2 irreducible classes. For a nonzero scalar only Y=0 is possible in odd characteristic. For the nonzero nilpotent block the compatible Y has diagonal (a,−a), lower-left zero, and free upper-right b; conjugation fixes a and shifts b by an arbitrary amount if a≠0, giving q+(q−1) orbits. For split nonzero trace zero, X has eigenvalues ±a and diagonal centralizer, with compatible off-diagonals (b,c) classified by the two nonzero axes, the origin and nonzero bc. For nonsplit trace zero, X=mθ on F_{q²}, θ^q=−θ; each linear map is uniquely z↦Az+Bz^q (evaluate at 1 and θ for uniqueness). Anticommutation sets A=0; the image of s↦s^(1−q) is the norm-one group (order q+1), giving one orbit per nonzero norm and the zero orbit. For nonzero trace and singular X, use diag(t,0) giving the q fixed Y=diag(0,b). For simultaneous nonzero trace and determinant the spectra of X and −X are disjoint, so the Sylvester map is invertible even for nonscalar Jordan X. Each allowable characteristic polynomial has exactly one nonscalar class, including the Jordan class when its roots repeat. These disjoint cases yield 4q²+q−2 for every odd prime power. A fresh enumeration using all of GL₂ in each tested field yielded 417 labeled pairs in 37 orbits for q=3 and 4705 in 103 for q=5 (replay: /workspace/branches/2c2c50d7-c13d-405a-ac11-d7ca67201f77/independent_orbit_bruteforce.py). The supplied verify.py was inspected, not run; both finite checks are restricted to prime fields and the general conclusion rests on the algebraic argument.

evidence: Chen–Wang and Chen–Lu describe geometric components and closed orbits in the GIT quotients. The Lopes–Lourenço representation hypotheses exclude roots of unity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The geometric quotient forgets nonclosed orbits, for example (nonzero nilpotent Jordan X,0) and (0,0) have the same closed orbit in their closures' quotient. It is not a classification of all orbits over finite fields. A representation theorem excluding roots of unity cannot be specialized to −1.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A Burnside computation based on the known labeled count would still require fixed-pair counts in the commutants of nonscalar conjugators; stabilizers vary. Neither the weighted sum nor closed-orbit geometry gives the nilpotent orbits or the distinction by quadratic field norm for fixed nonsplit X. The competing broader results do not imply the stated census as a specialization.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The observed 417 and 4705 are compatible with those known point counts. They are not the unweighted counts 37 and 103, nor does an all-arity point count table supply the per-X rational orbit classification.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is an explicit unweighted rational orbit census and its split/nonsplit classification in dimension two at deformation parameter −1. The known labeled count, complex geometric components and GIT-closed orbits are not credited as new. No inspected source supplies the full rational classification or unweighted invariant, and the assessment is bounded.
residual_risks: An uninspected specialized classification of root-of-unity quantum-plane modules over non-algebraically-closed fields could imply the rational census.

value.rationale: Dimension two is the first where nonzero anticommuting operators and nonsplit rational similarity occur; it is a natural base case for unweighted module enumeration at the sign parameter. An exact orbit count answers a different question from a weighted or point count and is accompanied by class invariants, in particular the norm rather than a split eigenbasis for nonsplit X. It provides an exact benchmark for rational classifications and distinguishes nonsemisimple classes that a GIT quotient loses. Neither an extension to larger dimensions nor a novel method of rational canonical forms is asserted.
